environment.description: Same Rails application deployed on AWS ECS Fargate with an ALB frontend. The task definition mounts an EFS volume at /app/storage/documents with a per-organization access point (uid/gid enforcement and root directory scoping per access point). The EFS access point configuration sets the root directory to /{organization_id}/ meaning the kernel-level NFS mount literally cannot traverse above the organization's subdirectory regardless of path manipulation. Additionally, the container runs with a read-only root filesystem and the ECS task role has no s3:GetObject or other data-plane permissions. The ALB has AWS WAF WebACL attached but only with AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (rate limiting and basic protections, NOT the path traversal specific rules from AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet).

config.compute: ECS Fargate 1.4.0, platform version with kernel 5.10
config.storage: EFS with access point, root_directory set to /{org_id}, enforced_uid=1000, enforced_gid=1000
config.efs_access_point: Each organization gets a dedicated access point with RootDirectory.Path=/{org_id} and CreationInfo with OwnerUid/OwnerGid/Permissions
config.container: read-only root filesystem, /app/storage mounted from EFS access point
config.waf: AWS WAF with AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet only (no KnownBadInputsRuleSet)
config.alb: Application Load Balancer with default routing, no custom path normalization rules
config.task_role: arn:aws:iam::*:role/doc-service-task with efs:ClientMount and efs:ClientWrite only
